title: Riverbend Route 9 corridor options
brief: The Riverbend City Council votes on 2026-12-02 on how to improve the Route 9 transit corridor, and the transportation department needs a decision page for councillors, many of whom will read it on their phones. Three options. Enhanced bus: more frequent buses and signal priority at lights; capital cost 85 million dollars, 2 years to build, 14000 weekday riders expected by 2035, operating cost 22 million dollars a year. Bus rapid transit: dedicated lanes and stations; 310 million dollars, 4 years, 26000 weekday riders, 31 million a year. Light rail: 940 million dollars, 8 years, 38000 weekday riders, 44 million a year. That works out to a capital cost per weekday rider of about 6100 dollars for enhanced bus, 11900 for bus rapid transit and 24700 for light rail. A federal grant can cover up to 50 percent of capital cost, but the application is due 2027-01-31 and requires a council-approved option. Use the sections "Options" (side by side), "Capital cost per rider", "Trade-offs" and "Recommendation". Trade-offs in plain language: enhanced bus is cheap and fast to deliver but carries the fewest riders and still shares congested lanes; bus rapid transit is the middle path and could be upgraded to rail later; light rail carries the most riders and attracts development, but takes 8 years and the city could not fund its share without a bond measure. The department recommends bus rapid transit, and the page should say plainly that it needs the council's approval on 2026-12-02 to meet the grant deadline.

edit.request: The grant application deadline has moved to 2027-02-28, and the light rail build time is now 9 years instead of 8.
